text: Coordination in computative settings runs through the interaction of generation functions rather than through a central coordinator, and this decentralization is structural rather than optional, since a central coordinator would itself be a computative agent generating an infinite regress.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Computative Economics A Framework for Economic Analysis under Computational Abundance (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6607458

isBasedOn.name: Computative Economics A Framework for Economic Analysis under Computational Abundance

abstract: The generative network is decentralized in the sense that coordination occurs through the interaction of generation functions rather than through a central coordinator. This property is structural rather than optional.
